topics.label: Introduction to cancer evolution and the lecture’s focus
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture by introducing cancer evolution and the roles of cell type and the microenvironment that it will examine.

topics.label: Mutation accumulation and clonal selection in cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These examples show how successive mutations can give clones a competitive advantage and drive their expansion through Darwinian selection.

topics.label: Epigenetic disruption as a driver of tumor development
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how transient changes in chromatin and gene transcription can contribute to tumor development even without new mutations.

topics.label: Stemness, cancer stem cells, and cell of origin
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how normal tissue hierarchies and stem-like properties relate to cancer initiation and tumor propagation.

topics.label: Inflammation and stemness in tumor initiation
topics.groupedBecause: Both examples show how inflammatory signals can provide conditions that help mutation-bearing cells acquire stem-like properties and form tumors.

topics.label: Microenvironmental support of established tumors and therapy
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic shows that established tumors can depend on supporting cells and explains how targeting those interactions may inform therapy.

topics.label: Single-cell and spatial methods for studying cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes sequencing and spatial profiling approaches used to study tumor evolution and interactions among cells.

topics.label: Integrated evolutionary model of cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic draws together the lecture’s evidence to argue that cancer outgrowth depends on mutations, cell properties, and a conducive environment acting together.

topics.label: Lecture close and next lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture and points to the subject of the next meeting.
